question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (seasonally adjusted), as it will be first reported in the Bank of England's monthly Money and Credit statistical release.

target.what: Number of net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom, seasonally adjusted, as first reported in the Bank of England's monthly Money and Credit statistical release for September 2026 (approvals net of cancellations, i.e. approvals minus cancellations within the month)
target.unit: net mortgage approvals for house purchase
target.publisher: Bank of England (Money and Credit statistical release)
target.caveats: Target period (September 2026) is completed relative to the 2026-10-27 cutoff, but the first official print is typically published around end-October/early-November, so the exact figure is likely not yet public at cutoff. Working interpretation: seasonally adjusted net approvals for house purchase (

candidates.perspective: BoE Money and Credit release archive
candidates.hypothesis: Net house-purchase approvals follow a persistent monthly level with modest month-to-month noise and a stable seasonal adjustment; recent months (mid-2026) plus the same month in prior years bracket the September 2026 value. Role: anchor level and trend.
candidates.data_to_find: BoE seasonally adjusted net mortgage approvals for house purchase (series LPMV4LT) for every month from Jan 2024 through the latest month published before 2026-10-27 (likely Aug 2026), plus September values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to gauge September seasonal position.
search_hints: Bank of England Money and Credit mortgage approvals September 2026
BoE LPMV4LT net mortgage approvals house purchase

candidates.perspective: UK Finance / trade body mortgage market data
candidates.hypothesis: UK Finance reports gross mortgage lending and house-purchase approvals/completions on a slightly different basis; its monthly approvals or lending figures correlate closely with BoE net approvals and can bridge to the target via a stable ratio. Role: independent level check and nowcast for September 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: UK Finance monthly house purchase approvals or gross lending for Jul-Sep 2026, and the historical ratio of BoE net approvals to UK Finance approvals/lending over 2024-2026.
search_hints: UK Finance house purchase approvals monthly 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Major lenders (Nationwide, Halifax, Barclays, Lloyds) and brokers report application volumes and approval pipelines; these lead BoE approvals by roughly one to two months and indicate direction of September activity. Role: directional nowcast and shock detection.
candidates.data_to_find: Lender/broker statements on mortgage application and approval volumes in Aug-Sep 2026, plus any reported changes in approval timescales or demand after base-rate or stamp-duty changes.
search_hints: mortgage approvals rise September 2026 UK lenders

candidates.hypothesis: Bank Rate changes, mortgage rate moves, stamp duty thresholds, and affordability rules shift approvals with a lag of one to three months; a rate cut or threshold change around mid-2026 would raise September approvals relative to trend. Role: adjust the own-history level for regime change.
candidates.data_to_find: BoE Bank Rate decisions and effective mortgage rates (2-year/5-year fixes) for Jun-Sep 2026; any UK stamp duty or Help-to-Buy policy changes effective 2026; ONS/BoE credit conditions survey signals.

candidates.hypothesis: City economists publish consensus forecasts for BoE mortgage approvals ahead of the release; these aggregate the same information set and provide a direct point estimate to compare against model routes. Role: benchmark and cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: Consensus/forecast for September 2026 UK net mortgage approvals (e.g. Reuters poll, Pantheon, Capital Economics, EY ITEM Club) published before 2026-10-27.
search_hints: UK mortgage approvals forecast September 2026 Reuters poll

candidates.hypothesis: Approvals convert to completions after a lag; HMRC residential transaction counts and RICS sales/agreed-sales indicators reflect the same underlying purchase flow and can constrain the approvals level via a stable approvals-to-completions ratio. Role: independent structural check.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly residential property transactions for mid-2026, RICS residential market survey new buyer enquiries/agreed sales for Aug-Sep 2026, and historical ratio of BoE approvals to completions.

candidates.hypothesis: September typically shows a modest seasonal uptick in purchase activity after summer; the SA series already removes this, but NSA-to-SA factors and working-day counts help validate whether a September print should sit above or below the August SA level. Role: refine month-to-month bridge.
candidates.data_to_find: BoE NSA net approvals for house purchase for recent Septembers and the implied SA factor; UK working days in September 2026 vs August 2026.
search_hints: BoE mortgage approvals non-seasonally adjusted September

plan_notes: plan proposed 7 candidate directions in 6 categories; running 7 (budget cap 10)

existing.note: not checked: the existing-figure step runs only in live use with a human at the approval step (not in backtests, scored, --auto-approve or ablation runs)

assessment.note: All report the same BoE August 2026 first print of 54,900 net house-purchase approvals; these are repeated syndications of one Bank of England release, not independent measurements.
Same BoE July 2026 revised figure of 55,900 across outlets; single underlying source.
August 54,900 and July 55,900 sit below the ~60,100 six-month average, consistent with a declining level through mid-2026.
May 2026 approvals around 56,200 on both the gbtt and calendar/consensus tables; consistent with the mid-2026 level.
April 2026 approvals ~65,900-66,000 across sources; the spring peak before the summer decline.
March 2026 first print 63,500, later revised to 64,000; illustrates revision magnitude of a few hundred.
February 2026 reported as 62,600 (intermediary) vs 62,700 (ii) vs 62,580 (calendar); minor vintage/rounding differences, not a real conflict.
September 2026 consensus 54,300 and TE model 54,500 are the same calendar-table entries duplicated; a single forecast source.
End-of-Q3 TE model expectation 59,100 is a quarterly model output, not a September point forecast; treat as weak context only.
Twenty7tec September 2026 purchase searches up 8% m/m but only 1% y/y, indicating flat rather than rebounding purchase demand.
RICS new buyer enquiries -22% in September, down from -18% in August; consistent across outlets, single RICS survey.
RICS agreed sales -18% in September vs -16% August; single survey source.
Mortgage valuations -7% y/y in August narrowing to -2% in September; suggests September activity slightly better than August y/y.
Sales agreed -11% y/y in Q3 2026; consistent with weak purchase flow.
HMRC SA transactions 95,220 in August, down 1% from 96,650 July; completions lag approvals by 2-4 months.
September 2025 approvals 65,900-65,944 across sources; the year-ago base for a y/y bridge.
Bank Rate held at 3.75% through September 2026; no rate-cut tailwind for September approvals.
Mortgage rates rising through September (2yr fix ~5.6-5.7%, new-mortgage average ~5.8%); a headwind for approvals.
Effective new-mortgage rate rose to 4.60% in August from 4.45% July; single BoE series.
FlexiAI autoregressive forecasts missed badly (July forecast 60,300 vs actual 56,100); last-value benchmark skill negative, so model forecasts are weak evidence.
Investing.com page dated 2016/2022 with undated rows; cannot be reliably aligned to months, so unusable for series construction.
Showhouse page dated 2025-10-30 labels September 2026 but reports 65,944 with +1.5% m/m and +0.5% y/y; internally inconsistent with the 2025 September print and mis-dated, so unusable.

assumptions.name: September 2026 to September 2025 approvals ratio
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 approvals were 65,900 (p16). Mid-2026 approvals have run well below year-ago levels: August 2026 54,900 vs August 2025 64,680 (p1 vs p127), a ratio of ~0.85; July 2026 55,900 vs July 2025 ~56,100-58,200, a ratio of ~0.96-1.0. The recent trend and rising mortgage rates (p478, p599) point to a ratio near 0.84, with a range reflecting the July/August spread.
assumptions.applies_when: The year-on-year ratio of September approvals is similar to the July-August 2026 ratio.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 approvals rebounded sharply toward the 2025 level, e.g. a consensus above 60,000.

assumptions.name: September 2026 to August 2026 approvals change factor
assumptions.rationale: The SA series already removes seasonality; Twenty7tec purchase searches rose 8% m/m in September (p324) but only 1% y/y (p325), and RICS new buyer enquiries weakened (p494). A flat-to-slightly-up month-on-month factor is consistent with these signals.
assumptions.applies_when: September SA approvals move broadly in line with August, as suggested by search and survey indicators.
assumptions.falsified_by: A strong September rebound or collapse in purchase searches or RICS agreed sales.

assumptions.applies_when: No large shock between August and September 2026.

methods.label: m1

p16.role: September 2025 net house-purchase approvals, seasonally adjusted, UK

a1.role: ratio of September 2026 to September 2025 approvals

methods.rationale: Year-on-year scaling from the September 2025 first print using a y/y ratio grounded in the 2026 market weakness (RICS negative, rates rising, approvals ~55k vs ~66k a year ago).

inputs_detail.name: p16
inputs_detail.unit: net mortgage approvals for house purchase

methods.label: m2

p1.role: August 2026 net house-purchase approvals, seasonally adjusted, UK

a2.role: month-on-month change factor from August to September 2026

methods.rationale: Month-on-month bridge from the August 2026 print, using the September consensus (54,300) and TE forecast (54,500) plus the modest positive search/valuation signals to justify a near-flat factor.

inputs_detail.name: p1
inputs_detail.unit: net mortgage approvals for house purchase

methods.label: m3

p110.role: consensus forecast for September 2026 UK mortgage approvals

methods.rationale: Direct consensus point estimate for the September 2026 print (54,300), the market's aggregate of the same information set; used as a benchmark route. Caveat: the same forecasters overshot August by ~1.2k, so this may be biased high relative to the eventual print.

kept.name: September 2026 to September 2025 approvals ratio
kept.rationale: September 2025 approvals were ~65,900 (p16). Recent 2026 levels (~55k) are ~16% below the year-ago base; RICS buyer enquiries and sales are negative, mortgage rates rising, so a y/y decline of ~16% is plausible. Range reflects uncertainty in the y/y gap.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 market weakness relative to 2025 persists into September 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September rebound (e.g. purchase searches up strongly y/y) would push the ratio toward 1.

kept.name: September 2026 to August 2026 approvals change factor
kept.rationale: August 2026 was 54,900 (p1); September consensus (p110) is 54,300 and TE forecast 54,500, implying a roughly flat-to-slightly-down month. Purchase searches +8% m/m (p324) and valuations improving (p292) suggest a small offsetting lift. Net: roughly flat.
kept.applies_when: No large shock between August and September 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A large September search or valuation surge/drop would move the factor outside the range.

The best estimate is 54,766 approval (80% model-based interval 38,759 to 77,384 approval) for net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom, seasonally adjusted, September 2026, as first reported in the Bank of England Money and Credit release.

Main evidence: the August 2026 print of 54,900 net mortgage approvals for house purchase anchors a near-flat month-on-month bridge (factor 1, range 0.8933 to 1.117), supported by the September consensus of 54,300 mortgage approvals for house purchase and modest positive search/valuation signals. A separate route scales the September 2025 print of 65,900 net mortgage approvals for house purchase by a year-on-year ratio of 0.84 (range 0.5925 to 1.185).

Observed: the August and September 2025 prints and the consensus. Assumed: both bridge factors. Code combined three blocks by equal weight per block, taking the median; the interval reflects the blocks' own widths.

Key risk: the consensus overshot August, so the flat bridge may be biased high. Better evidence would be early September approvals or timely lender data.

Unit of the estimate: approval (net mortgage approvals for house purchase; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 to September 2025 approvals ratio: 0.84 [n], range 0.5925 to 1.185 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp September rebound (e.g. purchase searches up strongly y/y) would push the ratio toward [n].
- a2 September 2026 to August 2026 approvals change factor: 1 [n], range 0.8933 to 1.117 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: A large September search or valuation surge/drop would move the factor outside the range.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p16 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 37,416 to 81,861; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: p1 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 44,437 to 67,980; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m3 formula_mc: p110; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 45,252 to 65,177; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 3 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 55,083 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: 54,766 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B3 = m3: 54,151 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.41; Birge ratio 0.03 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.41.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
